result.title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
result.summary: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate candidate capabilities. Then we suggest refining candidate capabilities so that they are testable in the context of AI systems. Finally, we offer specific empirical recommendations to test AI systems, especially large language models (LLMs), for those refined capabilities. Our approach offers several benefits. Firstly, it may demonstrate whether the behaviors of AI systems are aligned, or in a broad sense desirable. Secondly, the debate may inform policy questions (e.g., what models should be deployed in which contexts?). Thirdly, our approach may complement engineering and design efforts: when capabilities can be precisely characterized, they can inform the development of models. Fourthly, applying our moral reasoning concepts in the new context of AI systems should improve our understanding of those concepts.

AI.brief_summary: 论文从情感主义与理性主义两种哲学视角出发，提出一个描述性道德能动性研究纲领：先梳理人类道德能动性背后的候选能力，再将其细化为可在 AI 上检验的能力，并给出对 LLM 的实证测试建议。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文聚焦道德能动性的概念界定与哲学—心理学能力清单，未涉及视觉或多模态推理的内部状态、证据获取、计算分配或停止决策，也无可迁移至 LVR 的具体方法线索，故排除。
